newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-AUSTRALIA CURRENT ACCOUNT-Review of forecasts.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-AUSTRALIA CURRENT ACCOUNT-Review of forecasts.

text.p: Australia's current account deficit for December will be released at 11.30 a.m. (0130 GMT).
The median forecast of the 30 economists surveyed by Reuters is for a A$1.78 billion deficit.
Forecasts range from A$1.4 to A$2.0 billion.
The median expectation is under the A$1.923 billion shortfall posted in November, and only one of the economists surveyed expects the deficit to have increased in the month.
Previous months' data are detailed below.
Balance of Payments (s/adj, A$ million, current prices)
Jun Jul Aug Sep Oct Nov
Economists are forecasting a strong rebound in exports to drive the deficit down in the deficit. Exports fell in November, and have fallen 6.4 percent in the last three months.
Over the same period, a trade surplus of A$219 million has deteriorated to a deficit of A$394 million.
Data released earlier this month showed imports rose only 0.8 percent in December.
Once again the major contributor to the current account deficit will be the net income deifcit, which has been larger than the overall deficit for seven of the first 11 months of 1996.
There will be a touch of nostalgia associated with today's release -- it is expected to be the last monthly current account deficit in the current format.
In future, there will be a monthly trade and services update, and the current account deficit will be released quarterly.

The Australian Bureau of Statistics said this should improve the accuracy of the series because the current monthly net income deficit figures are extrapolations of quarterly data and subject to constant revision.
